Q: Open URL under cursor in Vim with browser A:

The following should fix the problem with a # character breaking the url in some of the other answers. After running the command below, just place the cursor somewhere on the url you want to open and type gx while in normal mode. The command below can be entered in normal mode or placed in your .vimrc file. A lot of credit goes to the other answers in this thread, which I used as basis:

Main Command:
nnoremap <silent>gx :sil execute '!start '.shellescape(matchstr(expand('<cWORD>'), 'https\?:\/\/[^[:space:]''">,;()`]\+'), 1) \| redraw!<cr>

If not on Windows, replace start with:

  • open if on macOS
  • cygstart if on a cygwin environment.
  • gnome-open/xdg-open if on linux.

Q: In SQL Server, why is searching for U+02B9 using LIKE statement match all strings, with or without that character? A:

The collation is used for the comparison and some characters are usually ignored. As mentioned in a comment use a binary collation like XXXXX_BIN2.

SELECT AString FROM
( SELECT N'abc' COLLATE Latin1_General_BIN2 AS AString) A
WHERE A.AString LIKE  N'%ʹ%';

Q: HDFS to HDFS move files force fully A:

HDFS shell commands doesn't support a -f for mv.

You will have to do the copy then remove method (as stated by you).

Q: iOS EAS Build Fails – “Distribution certificate hasn’t been imported successfully” A:

The instructions below have been tested on linux and windows with a successful Expo EAS App Store submission. In short, there are two major issues to get them to accept it: 1.) Apple needs their Apple Intermediate Certificate in the signing chain. In my case I used the Worldwide Developer Relations - G3 (Expiring 02/20/2030 00:00:00 UTC) in the chain to ensure trust has not been violated. I used G3 although other newer ones may work. 2.) For whatever reason legacy mode must be used as their system seems to be setup that way. Hope this helps you.

# Convert Apple WWDR cert (DER → PEM)
openssl x509 -inform DER -in AppleWWDRCAG3.cer -out AppleWWDRCAG3.crt

# Generate private key
openssl genrsa -out apple.key 2048

# Generate CSR
# works with powershell/cmd
openssl req -new -key apple.key -out apple.csr -subj "/emailAddress=<email>/CN=<common_name>"
# OR git bash windows
MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 openssl req -new -key apple.key -out apple.csr -subj "/emailAddress=<email>/CN=<common_name>"

# 👉 Upload apple.csr to Apple Developer → Certificates → Apple Distribution
# 👉 Download issued certificate which be your distribution.cer

# Convert cert + key + Apple chain → P12, make sure to use legacy
openssl pkcs12 -export -legacy \
  -inkey apple.key \
  -in distribution.cer \
  -certfile AppleWWDRCAG3.crt \
  -out distribution.p12

# NOTE: Any new or replaced distribution certificate requires regenerating the provisioning profile.
